Judgment

1 By this judgment I will dispose of appeal u/sec.374 Cr.PC. filed on behalf of convict Ajay Garg against the judgment dated 04.04.2014 and order on sentence dated 09.04.2014 passed by Sh.
Gaurav Rao, Ld. ACMM-II, Patiala House Court, New Delhi.
Ajay Garg Vs. State 2
The brief facts of the case as per record and from trial court record are that accused is running an establishment namely M/s Ajay Kumar & Co., Guru Angad Nagar Ext., Laxmi Nagar, Delhi-110092.
On 14.08.2002 at about 4.00 p.m. Food Inspector Sh. S. B. Sharma visited the said place and purchased 750 grams of "Dal Arhar" from accused.
FI was accompanied with SDM/LHA Sh. S. C. Tyagi.
The said Arhar Dal was purchased for the purposes of analysis under PFA Act.
The same sample was divided into three parts, packed as per Rules of PFA.
Panchanama was prepared.
One sample was sent for analysis to Public Analyst.
As per the report of Analyst, sample did not confirm to the standard because "The sample is adulterated because it is coloured with synthetic colouring matter viz. Tartrazine."
3 As the sample was failed, prosecution was launched by Food Inspector by filing complaint dated 18.02.2003 with the court.
Accused was summoned.
He has exercised his right u/sec.13(2) PFA Act to get the sample analyzed by CFL.

sentences.text: 5 After trial, vide judgment dated 04.04.2014 accused was convicted for offence u/sec.16(1A) of PFA Act and vide order on sentence dated 09.04.2014, accused was directed to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 18 months and fine of Rs.10,000/- and in default of payment of fine SI of 30 days.

6 In this appeal, the accused has assailed the judgment on the following grounds:-
(i) Non-compliance of Sec.10(7) of PFA Act and Rule i.e. independent witnesses were not joined.
(ii) Non-compliance of Rule 14 of PFA Rules i.e.
the bottles, jhawa, polythene were not made clean and dried at the spot by the food inspector or any other official (not specifically taken in appeal but argued orally).
(iii) Appellant is protected in view of Sec.19(2) PFA as he had established that he purchased the sample commodity from some other person and sold the same in the same condition.
7 No reply was filed by respondent/state and the matter was argued orally.
8 I have gone through the record, Trial Court record and have heard the submissions of Ld. counsel for appellant and Ld. SPP for State.
9 It is argued by counsel for appellant that no public Ajay Garg Vs. State  witness was present in the proceedings nor efforts were made to join any public witnesses.
As far as this argument is concerned, the same argument was raised before the Ld. Trial Court.
The same was dealt by the trial court from para 19 to 24 of the judgment.

As far as opinion/finding of the trial court regarding this argument is concerned, I do not find any infirmity in those findings and the same are upheld and the arguments regarding this fact does not find any force and thus rejected.

10 It is further argued that accused had purchased the sample commodity from Ramji Lal Narinder Kumar, Naya Bazar and sold the same in original condition, thus, appellant is protected u/sec.19(2)
PFA Act.

It is stated that on account of Sec.19(2) PFA Act, accused is protected against prosecution as it has established that the commodity was purchased from some other person and sold in the same condition.
This leg of arguments were dealt by the court from para 94 to 99.
I do not find any discrepancy/illegality in the reasoning given by trial court of this leg of argument.
Hence, the opinion given by the trial court in this regard is upheld.

sentences.text: It is further argued that compliance u/sec.14 PFA Rules was not proved on record by the prosecution.
It is stated that witnesses are deposing differently with respect to the cleanliness of jhaba etc.
It is further stated that it was the duty of the Ajay Garg Vs. State  prosecution to prove these facts.
It is further stated that there are discrepancies in the testimony of various witnesses.
These arguments were also addressed before the trial court.
The relevant part of the judgment dealing with these arguments are from para 25 to 40 (Rule 14 of PFA) and regarding discrepancies from para 41 to 55 of the judgment.

12 As far as the discrepancies are concerned, the court has given its opinion on the basis that even if there are minor discrepancies, if those does not goes to the root and are not substantial, it does not effect the case of the prosecution.
As far as the arguments in this regard is concerned, the law discussed by the trial court is correct and the same is self explanatory.
However, as far as the analysis of facts are concerned, to my opinion, the same requires some more elaboration.
13 As far as Rule 14 of PFA Rules are concerned, it spells out that the FI shall use dry bottles or containers for the purposes of sampling.

However, this fact was elaborated further by Hon. Supreme Court in Varghese Vs. Food, 1989 (II) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 236 stating that "it must be the endeavour of the FI to use clean and dry implements in sampling the articles of food.

entities.text: Varghese Vs. Food, 1989 (II) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If unhygienic methods are adopted, it will effect the result of analysis.
So, the Hon. Supreme Court use the Ajay Garg Vs. State word "implements" instead of only "dry and clean bottles/containers".

Similarly, in other judgments, i.e. State of Haryana Vs. Kishan Kumar CLT 559,
it was observed that the prosecution had not stated that the "weighing scale" was clean.

entities.text: State of Haryana Vs. Kishan Kumar CLT 559
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, in other judgments, like Sardar Mal Jain, 1996 (2) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 203, it was stated that the newspaper on which the Barfi was weighed was not clean.

entities.text: Sardar Mal Jain, 1996 (2) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 203
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, in Shashi Kant Vs. State of UP, 1983 (1) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases 90, it was observed that the "bhagona" was not proved to be clean and dry.

entities.text: Shashi Kant Vs. State of UP, 1983 (1) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases 90
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, in 2008 (3) RCR (Criminal) 422 Rajinder Kumar Vs. State of Haryana (Punjab and Haryana), it was held by the court that when an envelop is used for weighing the sample commodity, the same must be proved as clean and free from any impurity.

entities.text: 2008 (3) RCR (Criminal) 422 Rajinder Kumar Vs. State of Haryana (Punjab and Haryana)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14 So, accordingly, it can be said that the law which can be crystallized from various judgments of Hon. High Courts as well as Hon. Supreme Court is that if in evidence, the prosecution states that the sample commodity had touched a surface of an "implement", it is the duty of the prosecution to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the said implement was clean and dry and thus could not have added any impurity to the sample.
However, it is not the law that the FI shall spell out on which s u r f a c e s t h e s a m p l e c o m m o d i t y h a d t o u c h e d w h i l e s a m p l i n g .
H o w e v e r , i f h e
Ajay Garg Vs. State chooses to spell out the implements/surfaces with which the sample commodity came into contact/touch, the same must be proved as clean and dry.
15 In this case none of the witness except PW3 (cross- examination dated 30.04.2010) had deposed that the sample commodity was weighed by putting in a polythene bag.
He deposed "sample commodity was weighed after putting in polythene bag".

Nowhere it is deposed by any witness that Ajay Garg vs The State (Govt. Of Nct Of Delhi) on 4 August, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124192049/

16 So, in these circumstances, there is no proper compliance of Rule 14 PFA Rules.
The benefit goes in favour of appellant/convict.
17 So, the judgment and order on sentence of the trial court is reversed.
18 Accused Ajay Garg is acquitted of the charges u/sec.16(1A) read with sec.7 of PFA Act.
19 Bail Bond u/sec.437A Cr.P.C. furnished.
Accepted for six months.
20 TCR be sent back with copy of the order.
